'''Lawrence Kenneth Creamer''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|JP|FRSNZ|size=85%}} (23 October 1937 – 7 September 2019) was a New Zealand chemist specializing in milk protein chemistry. In 2004, he received the International Dairy Federation Award.

==Early life and education==
Born in [[Christchurch]] on 23 October 1937, Creamer was the son of Gladys Henrietta Creamer (née Hopkins) and William Henry Creamer.<Ref name="Death notice">{{cite news |url=https://deaths.dompost.co.nz/obituaries/dominion-post-nz/obituary.aspx?n=lawrence-creamer&pid=193849357 |title=Lawrence Creamer death notice |date=9 September 2019 |work=Dominion Post |accessdate=9 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://paperspast.natlib.govt.nz/newspapers/CHP19371025.2.2 |title=Births |date=25 October 1937 |work=The Press |page=1 |accessdate=9 September 2019}}</ref> He was educated at [[Christchurch Boys' High School]],<ref name="NZIC">{{cite news |url=https://nzic.org.nz/app/uploads/2018/10/Vol-42-No-1-March-1978.pdf |title=Branch officers 1977–78 |work=Chemistry in New Zealand |page=5 |volume=42 |issue=1 |date=March 1978 |accessdate=9 September 2019}}</ref> and went on to study chemistry at [[University of Canterbury|Canterbury University College]], graduating [[Master of Science]] with second-class honours in 1961.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university6.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: CO–Cu |website=Shadows of Time |accessdate=9 September 2019}}</ref> He completed a [[PhD]] at the same institution, by then called the [[University of Canterbury]], in 1963; the title of his doctoral thesis, supervised by Jack Vaughan and Alfred Fischer, was ''The Ladenburg rearrangement''.<ref name="NZIC"/><ref>{{cite thesis |last=Creamer |first=L.K. |type=PhD |title=The Ladenburg Effect |year=1963 |location=University of Canterbury |hdl=10092/9250 }}</ref><ref name="Scoop">{{cite news |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/BU0411/S00287/fonterra-scientist-awarded-top-dairy-honour.htm |title=Fonterra scientist awarded top dairy honour |work=Scoop Business |date=22 November 2004 |accessdate=9 September 2019}}</ref>

==Research career==
Creamer joined the New Zealand Dairy Research Institute (DRI), later part of [[Fonterra]], in [[Palmerston North]] in 1963, and between 1964 and 1966 he undertook protein research at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="NZIC"/> Returning to DRI, he rose to become a principal research scientist in 1990.<ref name="Scoop"/> He led a research team that investigated the chemistry of milk proteins and their interactions.<ref name="Scoop"/> His research covered both fundamental chemistry and practical aspects of the manufacturing of dairy products.<ref name="Scoop"/>

His early work resulted in improvements to the manufacture and consistency of cheese and milk powders.<ref name="Scoop"/> He carried out research into milk protein structures, and the effect of heat on milk and the aggregation of the proteins in whey.<ref name="Scoop"/> As a result, [[whey protein]]s, previously only used as animal feed, became ingredients in a range of food products.<ref name="Scoop"/> His research into casein hydrolysis in cheese led to greater understanding of the relationship between cheese composition, texture and flavour.<ref name="Scoop"/>

The current system under which New Zealand dairy farmers are paid for their milk based on its content of milk fat and protein solids was a direct result of work by Creamer.<ref name="Scoop"/>

From the 1990s, much of Creamer's research was on the structure of the whey protein [[Beta-lactoglobulin|β-lactoglobulin]], how it is affected by heat, and its ability to bind vitamins.<ref name="Scoop"/> His research found that the structure of β-lactoglobulin is altered at high temperature, forming a new protein that reacts with smaller milk proteins.<ref name="Scoop"/>

==Honours and awards==
In 1973, Creamer received the ICI New Zealand Prize, for outstanding achievement in chemical research, and the following year he was elected a Fellow of the New Zealand Institute of Chemistry.<ref name="NZIC"/> In 1984, the [[American Dairy Science Association]] awarded him the Miles-Marschall International ADSA Award, for research outside of North America leading to improved dairy products; he was, at the time, the youngest ever recipient of the award.<ref name="Scoop"/> Creamer was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1995,<ref name="Fellows">{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/organisation/academy/fellowship/fellows-1919-present/a-c/ |title=The Academy: A–C |date= |website= |publisher=Royal Society Te Apārangi |accessdate=9 September 2019}}</ref> and won the society's Scott Medal in 1999, for pre-eminence in fundamental, strategic and applied New Zealand dairy science and technology.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/scott-medal/recipients/ |title=Scott Medal |publisher=Royal Society Te Apārangi |accessdate=9 September 2019}}</ref> In 2004, Creamer received the world's top dairy honour, the International Dairy Federation Award, in recognition of his contributions to the dairy industry over more than 40 years.<ref name="Scoop"/>

==Death==
Creamer died in [[Wellington]] on 7 September 2019 at the age of 81.<ref name="Death notice"/>
